surprises.description: Q3 ARCALYST revenue was $286 million, well above the preview’s roughly $260 million consensus and its own $267 million estimate. The roughly $42–42.5 million sequential increase also far exceeded the preview’s modeled increase of about $23 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 ARCALYST revenue grew 58% year-over-year to $286 million, representing roughly $42-42.5 million in quarter-over-quarter growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (ARCALYST net product) | $260.2–260.7M”; “My Estimate | $267M”; the preview’s build showed Q2 revenue of $243.6M and Q3 estimate of $267.0M.

surprises.description: Kiniksa raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $1.045–$1.050 billion, above the preview’s expected raise to $1.000–$1.015 billion. The result positions ARCALYST to exceed $1 billion in annual revenue for the first time, while the preview described a $1.0 billion handle as the needed bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kiniksa raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.045 billion to $1.050 billion, positioning ARCALYST to exceed $1 billion in annual revenue for the first time.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 ARCALYST guidance | $980–995M (current) | Raise to $1.000–1.015B”; the preview said “Need a $1.0B handle.”

surprises.description: Operating and net income substantially exceeded the preview’s modeled results, while ARCALYST collaboration profit grew faster than sales. This contrasts with the preview’s concern that collaboration expense was rising as a share of sales and could constrain operating leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 operating income rose to $54.2 million and net income to $47.3 million”; “ARCALYST collaboration profit grew 67% to $211.6 million, outpacing sales growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Operating income” of “$33.1M” and “Net income” of “$29.3M,” and flagged collaboration expense as a swing factor, assuming it would rise to “36.5% of sales.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted meaningful ARCALYST prescribing among first-recurrence patients, an additional patient pool not quantified in the preview’s expectations, which centered on penetration of the 14,000-patient multiple-recurrence population.
surprises.fact_evidence: “About 20% of prescriptions already coming from the 26,000 annual first-recurrence patients.”

surprises.description: Management reported unusually large engagement increases from the Hearts Home DTC campaign, a marketing result the preview did not discuss or set an expectation for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Hearts Home DTC campaign drove a 12-fold increase in ARCALYST website traffic and an eightfold increase in engaged sessions, with roughly 55% of ad viewers motivated to speak with their healthcare provider.”
